label: Seventeen French vessels were reported at Bantry Bay.
Most vessels were described as dismasted.
People landing were said to have been imprisoned and sent/went to Dublin.
The writer predicted the whole force must inevitably be captured.
The intended landing was said to be Londonderry.
The CHRONICLE annotation challenges dates, route and numbers.
A later summary says the main body returned to Brest in divisions without material loss.
The Peace, cargo and specie were reported condemned at a value of $25,000.
The stated pretext for seizure was arrival from a British port.
The printed Cayenne decree translation cites American newspaper dates.
The translation authorizes seizures involving British ports and vague destinations.
An editorial note alleges seven of eight cited instances were false.
The clearance resolution was approved on 7 May 1794.
Loaded US-owned vessels bound beyond the Cape could be cleared subject to the resolution.
Owners had to provide security against unloading before reaching the Cape.
